1  JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30-09-2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 30-09-2024 at about 2.00 a.m.,the petitioner was traveling in Tata AC Sleeper coach Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 from Bengaluru to Chennai NH road, while bus reached near Nekkundhi village, at that time the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53- 2458 has parked the lorry on the road without any indicator or signal and without keeping any safety cone beside the lorry had parked on the road negligently, meanwhile the driver of the bus hit the lorry from behind, and caused the accident.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government hospital,
Vaniyambadi wherein first aid treatment was given, thereafter petitioner was shifted to Atreum Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment and underwent surgery.

Petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and working as Software Engineer at Excelencia iTech Consulting and earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and suffered loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3.

In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1- owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence placed exparte.
After service of notice, the respondent No.2-insurer appeared through its counsel.

Respondent No.2 - insurance company has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Lorry bearing No. KA.53-2458 and the liability of this respondent is any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the policy was valid at the time of accident.

It has specifically submitted that the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties to the proceedings i.e.,
the owner and insurer of the Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 not made as party to the proceedings.
Hence it is required to direct the claimant to implead the same as party to the proceedings in order to adjudicate the matter factually and effectually.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.

Further it has contended that, the respondent No.1 owner has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license and the vehicle was not having Rakeshkumar C.T vs Shafiulla on 20 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164902602/

Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the ac- cident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 and as a result, he sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the petitioners as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for com- pensation? If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
5.

Further, examined the Orthopedic Doctor at Atreum Hospital, Bengaluru and Dr. Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic surgeon at SOADS hospital as PW.2 and 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.22 & 23.
6.

In support of his case, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, IMV report wound certificate, charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 5.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR which is registered on the basis of first information statement given by one Balamurugan who is the driver of the bus in which the petitioner traveling as a passenger.

In continuation of Ex.P1, the IO prepared IMV reports of both the vehicles involved in the accident which are marked as Ex.P2 and 3 shows that offending Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 has got damages i.e., left side and rear load body broken, left side rear chassis frame, rear cross bar bent, both tail lamps broken, left side rear stepny bracket damaged and the Bus bearing No.KA-59-9666 has got damaged to right side front body torn out and pressed inward upto right side 1st window, both lower and upper berth damaged, right side front window glass broken, right side driver seat, steering assembly, dash board broken and pressed inward, right side air filter broken, front bumper broken, right side front cross bar bent, front wind sheild glass broken, right side front head light indicator broken, right side top body torn out, front right side body show set broken, right side front wheel cover broken, right side front tie rod bent, right side front platform bent, right side rear view mirror broken, right side EC board assembly broken, right side front wirings damaged, right side driver door pressed inward.

The contents of Ex.P2, and P3 supported the case of the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 who parked his vehicle in the middle of the road.

10. The charge sheet as per Ex.P5 is filed against the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53- 2458 wherein the IO opined that negligent parking by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53- 2458 was the sole reason for the accident.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:

But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants''.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 5 & 10,
this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the negligent parking by the driver of Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458.

11. The respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 .
Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the negligent parking by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458 .
12. The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the negligent parking by the driver of the offending lorry.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

The main cause for the accident is the negligent parking of the lorry in the middle of the road.

No evidence is available to consider that the said offending lorry was parked in the road by taking safety Rakeshkumar C.T vs Shafiulla on 20 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164902602/

15. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 30.09.2022 which is caused by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA- 53-2458 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 & 3:
These two issues are interlinked each other in respect of the entitlement of the petitioner in claiming compensation, hence, they are taken together for common discussion.
16. As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 27 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P12 shows the date of birth of the petitioner as 24-03-1995, the accident was occurred on 30-09-2022, as on the date of accident petitioner was aged about 27 years.

In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, Vaniyambadi and for further treatment shifted Atreum hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P6 the petitioner was admitted to Atreum hospital as an inpatient from 30-09-2022 to 10- 10-2022 and sustained comminuted fracture of left proximal tibia.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.50,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10, amounting to Rs.2,22,465/-.
At the time of cross-examination the suggestions were made by suggesting that the serial No.24, 28, 29, 33, 36, 38 and 39 are created.
On perusal of the said serial number bills, merely because these bills are hand written bills they cannot be said as created.
The prescriptions in support of these bills are also produced.
Coming to the Serial Nos.42 bill in Ex.P10 bill i.e., inpatient bill of Rs.1,27,190/- supported with the discharge summary and prescriptions.
The advance paid receipts are also produced along with payments made through card.
Hence, no grounds are made out to disbelieve the said bill also.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.2,22,500/-.

6 c) Loss of income during laid up period and future loss of income:

To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS Hospital as PW.3 and through him clinical notes and X-ray were got marked at Ex.P22 & 23.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained Type I open comminuted fracture of the left proximal tibia.
He has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and the petitioner has suffered total disability of 40% at left lower limb and whole body at 13%.
When the PW.3 cross-examined he has stated that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are healing and muscle strength can be regained through physiotherapy and also there is no complication.

Thereby by keeping the answers given by the PW.3 in the cross-examination it is necessary to verify whether after the healing period when the loss and wastage of muscle can be regained through physiotherapy whether the petitioner has really has permanent disabilities which effects his occupation or not has to be looked into.
No doubt that the PW.3 doctor examined the petitioner and assessed the physical disability.
As per the evidence of Pw.3 doctor the petitioner has sustained Type I open comminuted fracture of the left proximal tibia.
As per the evidence of PW.3 as admitted in the cross-examination the loss of strength can be regained through physiotherapy.
In this case, as stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident he was getting salary of Rs.95,000/- and now he is working at HCL company and getting salary of Rs.91,000/-.
The nature of the job of the petitioner is not affected by the injuries sustained by the petitioner in RTA.
As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the loss of strength can be regained by the petitioner by physiotherapy and the wounds are healed.
Thereby there is no specific evidence to show that due to the injury sustained in RTA the petitioner was unable to attend his work after the recovery.

As admitted by the PW.3 doctor the healing period was four months and after the said four months, no evidence is available to hold that due to the said injury the petitioner has lost his working capacity.
The answers given by the PW1 clearly states that presently the petitioner is working and he is continued with his profession.

In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 1449-2023 connected with 3330-2023 between Iffco Tokio Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., V/s. Smt. Jayashree and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when there is no exact evidence to show that due to the injuries the petitioner has lost working capacity, the consideration of loss of future income due to disability does not arise.

As the petitioner continued with service and he has not suffered any financial loss.

7 e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P6 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 11 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 11 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.11,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 11 days in the hospital.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The evidence of Pw3 doctor reveals that there is a restriction of movements and also physical disability to some extent in mobility and stability components.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Future medical expenses:

Petitioner has examined Dr. Nikhil S., Orthopedic surgeon at Atreum Hospital, Bengaluru and in his evidence he has stated that petitioner needs to undergo surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.4,50,000/-.
But no estimation is produced in this regard.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 50,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,22,500/-
c. Towards loss of income during NIL  laid up period d.
Towards disability NIL e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 40,000/-
 conveyance f.

Towards attendant charges Rs. 11,000/-
g.

Towards loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 1,00,000/-
Liability:-

According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending Ashok Leyland Lorry Rakeshkumar C.T vs Shafiulla on 20 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164902602/

The respondent No.2 insurance company in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy condition by the respondent No.1 owner.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 owner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
18.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,53,500/-
(Rupees Four lakhs fifty three thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
(excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 5 & 10,
this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the negligent parking by the driver of Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA-53-2458.
12. The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the negligent parking by the driver of the offending lorry.
The respondent no.2 even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
13. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
15. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 30.09.2022 which is caused by the driver of the Ashok Leyland Lorry bearing No.KA- 53-2458 which belonging to respondent No.1.
No doubt that the PW.3 doctor examined the petitioner and assessed the physical disability.
As per the evidence of Pw.3 doctor the petitioner has sustained Type I open comminuted fracture of the left proximal tibia.
The nature of the job of the petitioner is not affected by the injuries sustained by the petitioner in RTA.
As admitted by the PW.2 doctor the loss of strength can be regained by the petitioner by physiotherapy and the wounds are healed.
Thereby there is no specific evidence to show that due to the injury sustained in RTA the petitioner was unable to attend his work after the recovery.
As admitted by the PW.3 doctor the healing period was four months and after the said four months, no evidence is available to hold that due to the said injury the petitioner has lost his working capacity.
In the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka 1449-2023 connected with 3330-2023 between Iffco Tokio Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., V/s. Smt. Jayashree and another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that when there is no exact evidence to show that due to the injuries the petitioner has lost working capacity, the consideration of loss of future income due to disability does not arise.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The learned counsel for respondent No.2-insurance company relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in between Sri.Subash V/s The New India Assurance Company Ltd., Represented by its Manager and Others wherein held that, "If the claimant is continued in service, then, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise."
As the petitioner continued with service and he has not suffered any financial loss.
No evidence is also placed by showing that he has not received any salary during the laid up period.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitle for compensation under these head.

Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 50,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,22,500/-
c. Towards loss of income during NIL  laid up period d.
Towards disability NIL e.
Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 40,000/-
 conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 11,000/-
g.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 1,00,000/-
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1 owner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.4,53,500/-
(Rupees Four lakhs fifty three thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
(excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
